item.title: #3594337: Add a command to export configuration
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +325/−0 · php +325
  • Diff: 1e10d0d
  • Discussion: #3594337 · 5 contributors · 15 comments
  • Followers: 12
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

Drupal core's dr command line tool gains a config:export command. It writes the site's active configuration into the configured sync directory, matching what the Configuration UI export produces. It shows a table of what will be created, updated, deleted or renamed, and asks for confirmation unless --yes (-y) is passed. If the sync directory already matches, it reports that and does nothing. This is part of the CLI in Core initiative (#3582246) and is useful for deployment workflows and keeping config in source control.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New config:export console command (Drupal\Core\Config\Command\ConfigExportCommand, marked @internal) run via dr config:export, with a --yes/-y option.

Technical details

ConfigExportCommand is registered with #[AsCommand(name: 'config:export')] and autowires the config.storage.export service, the same export storage the UI uses. Because of that, config overrides (such as $config settings overrides) are not exported, and export transformers (for example from config_transformer_test in the tests) are applied. It also takes the SyncFactory service. The sync storage is resolved inside __invoke() rather than the constructor. SyncFactory::get() throws ConfigDirectoryNotDefinedException when no sync directory is configured, and a throwing constructor would break dr list for every command. The command catches that exception, prints the message and returns FAILURE.\n\nA StorageComparer between export and sync storage builds the changelist. With no changes it prints a success message and exits. Otherwise renderTable() prints Collection, Config and Operation columns, with renames shown as old -> new. After confirmation the command calls replaceStorageContents() from StorageCopyTrait, which replaces the sync contents with the export. Declining the confirmation throws UserAbortException. A kernel test, ConfigExportCommandTest, covers the missing directory case, --yes, the no-changes case, cancelling, and transformers being applied. A PHPStan baseline entry was added for the missing return type on replaceStorageContents().

item.title: #3594336: Add a command to list modules and themes on a site
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +226/−0 · php +226
  • Diff: 5f4a8ff
  • Discussion: #3594336 · 8 contributors · 27 comments
  • Followers: 13
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 8 contributors

Summary

Drupal core's console (dr) gets an ex:list command that lists the modules and themes on a site. The output is a table of package, name (with machine name), install status and version. It can instead be printed as JSON or YAML. Filter options narrow the list by extension type, core or non-core, package and install status. It is the counterpart of Drush's pm:list, and it is part of the CLI in Core initiative (#3582246).

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New Drupal\Core\Command\OutputFormat enum (Yaml, Json) for console command output formats.

Technical details

The command is Drupal\Core\Extension\Command\ExtensionListCommand, marked @internal and declared with the #[AsCommand] attribute. Its options use Symfony's #[Option] attributes: --core/--no-core, --type (the existing ExtensionType enum), --package (comma delimited, case insensitive), --installed/--no-installed and --format. It merges the lists from ModuleExtensionList and ThemeExtensionList. It always skips extensions whose path contains tests. The --core filter relies on $extension->origin, which themes lack, so there is a @todo pointing to #3605703. Without --format the output is a Symfony Table. With it, the rows are encoded by json_encode() or Yaml::encode(), using the new Drupal\Core\Command\OutputFormat backed enum. The command is registered under ex:list and currently also carries the aliases pm:list and pml. A reviewer (see collaboration) suggested replacing these with exl. Table formatting and line length were left to #3611694. Making OutputFormat extensible is tracked in #3629792. A kernel test, ExtensionListCommandTest, covers the JSON output, the filters and the table output.

item.title: #3575642: Always free up old container on rebuild, not only in the installer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +62/−19 · php +62/−19
  • Diff: 7336168
  • Discussion: #3575642 · 7 contributors · 30 comments
  • Followers: 18
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 7 contributors

Summary

Rebuilding the service container, for example when modules are installed or uninstalled during update hooks, used to keep the old container and everything it referenced in memory. Core already fixed this for the installer only. It now applies on every rebuild. The reporter saw an update that installs and uninstalls several modules grow to 666MB. With the change it stayed at roughly 300MB or less. Sites that hit the error You have requested a synthetic service ("kernel") when modules with injected hook classes (such as pathauto) were enabled also reported that the merge request fixed it.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: DrupalKernel::attachSynthetic() now resets the previous container, and Container::reset() and PhpArrayContainer::reset() keep synthetic services (and request_stack) instead of clearing everything. The InstallerKernel::attachSynthetic() override is removed.

Technical details

DrupalKernel::attachSynthetic() now calls $this->container?->reset() on the previous container after attaching synthetic services to the new one. This replaces the override that previously lived only in InstallerKernel, which is deleted. The old reset() simply emptied $services. Calling it on every rebuild would have dropped synthetic services such as kernel and keyvalue, which can't be built by the container. That is what caused the synthetic service exceptions in tests. Container::reset() and PhpArrayContainer::reset() now clear private services and unset only non-synthetic services, and they always keep request_stack. request_stack is not synthetic but must not be reset. PhpArrayContainer checks the synthetic key in the definition, which may be a serialized string. Container checks isSynthetic().\n\nBecause the old container is now reset, objects that outlive a rebuild can no longer rely on it. ModuleInstaller::updateKernel() records the service IDs of its uninstallValidators through ReverseContainer::getId() before the rebuild. Afterwards it replaces them with a RewindableGenerator that fetches the same services from the new container. MimeTypeGuesser::registerWithSymfonyGuesser() moves from DrupalKernel::preHandle() to initializeContainer(), so Symfony's static MIME guesser is re-registered with the new container on each rebuild. In the thread, the concern was that this call is on the early critical path before a page cache hit. Following up by adding MimeTypeGuesser to the early bootstrap autoload classmap was deferred to #3612177. The diff also includes a comment update in a router installer test.

Upgrade

Custom code that caches services in properties across a container rebuild, such as module installs or updates inside one request, may now hold services from a reset container. Re-fetch them from \Drupal::getContainer() after the rebuild, as ModuleInstaller::updateKernel() now does for its moduleHandler, connection, updateRegistry and uninstallValidators. Tests that persist services with injected dependencies, such as event dispatchers registered via register(), may need adjusting.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: February 25, 2026
  • Committed: October 9, 2026 (7 months later)

Key contributors

  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • catch (Third and Grove)
  • godotislate
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • tlo405

Collaboration

berdir first moved the installer-only reset into the base kernel, but it broke many tests. After discussion he switched to a soft reset that keeps synthetic services. godotislate suggested using the reverse container to look up the uninstall validators' service IDs and rebuild them after the rebuild, which led to the ModuleInstaller::updateKernel() change. alexpott questioned the MimeTypeGuesser move, and berdir explained it is there because a rebuild re-registers the guesser.

item.title: #3625895: Deprecate and remove Query::__wakeup() and ::__sleep()
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +24/−17 · php +24/−17
  • Diff: c305d65
  • Discussion: #3625895 · 6 contributors · 18 comments
  • Followers: 8
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 6 contributors

Summary

Database query objects (Select, Insert and so on) can no longer be serialized or unserialized on the main branch (12.x). Attempting it now throws a LogicException. On 11.5.x the same methods were deprecated rather than removed, so custom or contrib code that serializes a query, or an object holding one, gets a deprecation notice there and should stop. Core itself does not do this anywhere.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Query::__sleep() and Query::__wakeup() removed in 12.x; Query serialization and unserialization now throw \LogicException (deprecated in 11.5.0 on the 11.x branches).
  • Deprecation: Query::__sleep() and Query::__wakeup() are deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 and removed from drupal:12.0.0.

Technical details

Query::__sleep() and Query::__wakeup() are replaced in Drupal\Core\Database\Query\Query by __serialize() and __unserialize(), which both throw \LogicException. The old __wakeup() reattached an unserialized query to whatever connection Database::getConnection($this->connectionTarget, $this->connectionKey) returned at the time, with no guarantee that connection was the right one. This was inconsistent with Connection, which already refuses serialization (#2463321), and with PDO. The change also finishes off #2463321. The now-unused Database import is removed. SerializeQueryTest is rewritten to assert that serialize() and unserialize() throw. Per the thread, the full test suite showed nothing in core round-trips a query apart from that one test. The commit landed on main and 12.0.x as a hard removal. On 11.x and 11.5.x it landed as a deprecation, with the deprecation version being 11.5.0 and removal in 12.0.0, pointing to change record https://www.drupal.org/node/3625908. I only read the main diff, so the 11.5.x deprecation details come from the reviewer comment on MR !17239. #3548971 (replacing __sleep()/__wakeup() with __serialize()/__unserialize()) is the related issue, and this change means Query no longer needs converting there.

Upgrade

Stop serializing query objects, and objects that hold references to them. Store the query arguments or the results instead. The exception message says: "Adjust your code so that is not necessary, for example by storing the query arguments or results instead."

Contribution

  • Opened: September 25, 2026
  • Committed: October 8, 2026 (13 days later)

item.title: #1411074: Allow kernel tests to share the test environment
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 36 files, +1261/−145 · php +1261/−145
  • Diff: 47430c3
  • Discussion: #1411074 · 23 contributors · 138 comments
  • Followers: 47

Summary

Kernel test classes can now opt in to sharing one database across all their test methods with the #[ShareEnvironment] attribute. The schema, config and other initial state are built once per class instead of once per method, which speeds up classes with many methods (the issue reports roughly 20 to 40 percent of total time). Classes without the attribute behave exactly as before. In core, the config entity validation tests were converted as the first users. Converting the rest of core's Kernel tests, and later making sharing the default in the next major, are follow-ups. The change was also backported to 11.x and 11.5.x so contrib can adopt it.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: ConfigEntityValidationTestBase now builds its entity in setUpEnvironment() and reloads it in setUp() for shared classes. Core subclasses were converted from setUp() to setUpEnvironment().
  • New API: New Drupal\TestTools\Attribute\ShareEnvironment attribute, plus KernelTestBase::setUpEnvironment(), resetEnvironment() and sharesEnvironment().

Technical details

The attribute is not inherited: ShareEnvironment::isEnabledFor() reflects on the concrete class only, and #[ShareEnvironment(FALSE)] marks a class as needing its own environment. For an opted-in class, a #[BeforeClass] hook (allocateSharedDatabase()) reserves one database prefix with a locked TestDatabase and passes it to the forked per-method processes through the DRUPAL_TEST_SHARED_DB_PREFIX environment variable. An #[AfterClass] hook drops all the tables and releases the lock. PHPUnit's #[RunTestsInSeparateProcesses] is still in effect, so each method still has its own process, container and virtual file system. Only database state is shared.\n\nIn bootKernel() the first method calls the new setUpEnvironment() hook (empty by default), then records the table list and a ready row in a test_shared_database_state table. Later methods skip the hook. If the hook fails, or a method breaks the shared state, the state is marked invalid and the remaining methods fail with the recorded reason. For shared classes the keyvalue service is a KeyValueDatabaseFactory instead of the in-memory factory, so entity definitions and state persist with the tables. core.extension is rewritten per method with the module list rebuilt but the installed themes kept.\n\nThe old tearDown() table-dropping logic moved to resetEnvironment(), which does nothing for shared classes. Instead tearDownEnvironment() fails the method if it dropped a shared table or left a new table behind. INFRASTRUCTURE_TABLES (currently cache_container) is exempt, and a class can redeclare it. Test methods must not assume a clean database, and tables they create must be removed in resetEnvironment(). ConfigEntityValidationTestBase was adapted: shared subclasses build $this->entity in setUpEnvironment(), and the base setUp() records and reloads the entity from the key value store. Unconverted subclasses that assign $this->entity in setUp() still work. A change record is at node 3623403, and follow-ups are #3623409 (add the attribute to all Kernel tests) and #3623410 (make sharing the default). #3613347 (re-use the container) builds on this.

Upgrade

To opt a Kernel test class in, add the attribute and move fixture creation from setUp() to setUpEnvironment(), as the converted core tests do:

use Drupal\TestTools\Attribute\ShareEnvironment;

#[RunTestsInSeparateProcesses]
#[ShareEnvironment]
class ActionValidationTest extends ConfigEntityValidationTestBase {

  protected function setUpEnvironment(): void {
    parent::setUpEnvironment();
    // Build the shared fixture here.
  }

}

Remove tables or other state a test method adds by overriding resetEnvironment() and calling the parent.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: January 20, 2012
  • Committed: October 6, 2026 (14 years later)

Key contributors

  • sun
  • tstoeckler
  • mile23 (CivicActions)
  • moshe weitzman
  • catch (Third and Grove)
  • amateescu
  • mstrelan (PreviousNext)

Collaboration

plach reworked the issue from per-method database setup toward a shared-environment approach. After benchmarking an experimental MR he dropped a complex database-reset mechanism in favor of an opt-in model, once he found few classes needed it. catch contributed the container re-use idea (split into #3613347) and pushed for simpler semantics, and the two settled on the #[ShareEnvironment] attribute, which preserves BC and leaves room to flip the default in the next major.

item.title: #3344629: Passing null to parameter #1 ($haystack) of type string is deprecated
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +75/−3 · php +75/−3
  • Diff: 9493974
  • Discussion: #3344629 · 16 contributors · 64 comments
  • Followers: 21
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 16 contributors

Summary

Three response subscribers no longer trigger "Passing null to parameter #1 ($haystack) of type string is deprecated" when a response carries a Content-Type header whose value is NULL. This showed up as unsilenced deprecations in PHPUnit runs (for example the Gatsby module's kernel test), as image generation problems for a site using a webp convert effect, and as failing contrib tests such as JSON:API Extras. Anonymous access to a Views data export that required authentication also triggered it. Those responses are now skipped by the subscribers, as any non-matching content type would be.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

HeaderBag::get('Content-Type', '') returns NULL, not the default, when the header exists with a [null] value, so the '' default did not protect stripos() and str_contains(). The fix changes the call to $response->headers->get('Content-Type') ?? '' in ActiveLinkResponseFilter, RssResponseRelativeUrlFilter and the JSON:API ResourceResponseValidator. The root cause, discussed in the thread, is that Request::getMimeType() returns NULL when the format is not registered in Request::$formats. Drupal normally registers formats in NegotiationMiddleware::handle(). The JSON:API, REST and serialization subscribers then call headers->set('Content-Type', NULL). Response::prepare() cannot repair this because it only acts when the header is absent. Tightening those writers was left for a follow-up, since it would change behavior (no header versus an empty one). Tests were added: ResourceResponseValidatorTest::testOnResponseNullContentType() and an ActiveLinkResponseFilter unit test that promotes E_DEPRECATED to an exception.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: February 27, 2023
  • Committed: October 5, 2026 (3 years later)

Key contributors

  • jaykumar95 (ByteParity)
  • Kaushik1216 (Google Summer of Code)
  • bbrala (SWIS)
  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • sweetchuck
  • akram khan (Material)
  • f0ns (Webhaven)
  • larowlan (PreviousNext)

Collaboration

Reviewers asked what sets the header to NULL, and larowlan pointed at the getMimeType() callers in the JSON:API and REST subscribers. f0ns traced the cause through Request::getMimeType(), HeaderBag::set() and Response::prepare(), and showed why a NULL-safe read is needed regardless. The test-only run initially did not fail. f0ns reworked the ActiveLinkResponseFilter test, which lives in core/lib, so it fails when the fix is reverted.

item.title: #3626105: Release runtime theme registries after destruction
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +26/−1 · php +26/−1
  • Diff: 96cfe41
  • Discussion: #3626105 · 4 contributors · 11 comments
  • Followers: 7
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 4 contributors

Summary

On persistent PHP workers such as FrankenPHP in worker mode, the theme registry service can outlive a request. After the first request's cleanup, later requests could log "Theme hook %hook not found." and render nothing for the affected hooks. The registry now discards its runtime collectors during cleanup, so the next request gets fresh ones and theme hooks are found again. Sites on classic PHP-FPM or Apache are not affected.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Registry::destruct() called destruct() on each collector in $this->runtimeRegistry but kept them. CacheCollector::destruct() persists pending changes and resets storage. Registry::getRuntime() then returned the same retained, emptied ThemeRegistry, whose has() and get() read that storage directly. So previously registered hooks came back as missing, and ThemeManager::render() logged the "not found" message and returned FALSE.

The fix copies $this->runtimeRegistry to a local variable, sets the property to [], then destructs the copies. The next getRuntime() call builds a new ThemeRegistry, whose constructor loads the runtime cache or initializes on a miss. Repeated destruct() calls also skip collectors that were already processed. A new kernel test, testRuntimeRegistryAfterDestruct() in RegistryTest, checks that a hook is still found after destruct() and that a different collector instance is returned. The committer noted that for persistent workers it may be better not to clean up these collectors at all, so a loaded registry stays available across requests. That is left for later work.

item.title: #3568767: Deprecate Media::getRequestTime()
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +12/−9 · php +12/−9
  • Discussion: #3568767 · 5 contributors · 28 comments
  • Followers: 6
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

The Media entity's getRequestTime() method, previously undocumented beyond a generic {@inheritdoc} comment despite not actually overriding anything, is now deprecated with no replacement. The method will be removed in Drupal 13. It is no longer used internally by Drupal core, so most sites are unaffected; only code that explicitly calls Media::getRequestTime() needs to change.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Media::getRequestTime() is deprecated in drupal:12.1.0 and removed from drupal:13.0.0, with no replacement.

Technical details

The created base field on the Media entity used Media::getRequestTime() as its setDefaultValueCallback(), even though the method simply returned \Drupal::time()->getRequestTime(), the same value the created field type (CreatedItem::applyDefaultValue()) already sets by default. Since the callback was redundant, it was removed from Media::baseFieldDefinitions() entirely rather than just documented, and the method itself was marked @deprecated with a proper docblock, a return type hint (: int), and a trigger_error() call pointing to the change record at https://www.drupal.org/node/3624921. The corresponding PHPStan baseline entry for the method's missing return type was also removed since the new return type hint makes it unnecessary.

Upgrade

Replace any direct calls to the deprecated method:

// Before:
$time = Media::getRequestTime();

// After:
$time = \Drupal::time()->getRequestTime();

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: January 21, 2026

Key contributors

  • avpaderno
  • dcam
  • catch (Third and Grove)

Collaboration

What started as a documentation-only fix changed direction after catch pointed out that getRequestTime() wasn't needed at all, since CreatedItem already defaults the created field to the request time without it; this prompted removing the setDefaultValueCallback() usage and deprecating the method instead of just documenting it. Later, catch also caught that the deprecation's target version needed updating once Drupal 12.0.x opened, which avpaderno corrected to drupal:12.1.0 after initially targeting the wrong release.

item.title: #3081025: Remove technical debt and complication from when doTrustedCallback() could either trigger errors or throw exceptions
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +57/−44 · php +57/−44
  • Diff: de58972
  • Discussion: #3081025 · 9 contributors · 39 comments
  • Followers: 14
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 9 contributors

Summary

When Drupal detects an "untrusted" callback (for example in a render array), it now always throws an exception rather than offering an option to only log a silenced deprecation warning instead. This closes a long-standing loophole left over from the original security hardening work in #2966327: Drupal core itself has thrown the exception unconditionally since Drupal 9, but the old $error_type escape hatch was still present in the API for anyone who wanted to opt into the softer, warning-only behavior. That option is now deprecated and will disappear in Drupal 13.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: TrustedCallbackInterface::THROW_EXCEPTION and TrustedCallbackInterface::TRIGGER_SILENCED_DEPRECATION are deprecated, and the $error_type parameter of DoTrustedCallbackTrait::doTrustedCallback() / StaticTrustedCallbackHelper::callback() is removed from the method signature; passing a 5th argument now triggers a deprecation notice and is removed in Drupal 13.0.0.

Technical details

DoTrustedCallbackTrait::doTrustedCallback() and StaticTrustedCallbackHelper::callback() dropped the $error_type parameter from their signatures; the method body no longer branches on TRIGGER_SILENCED_DEPRECATION and simply throws Drupal\Core\Security\UntrustedCallbackException whenever a callback fails the trusted-callback check. Renderer::doCallback() was updated accordingly to call doTrustedCallback() without an error-type argument.

Because $extra_trusted_interface was the 5th parameter and $error_type the 4th, removing $error_type from the signature would silently break any caller still passing both. To preserve backward compatibility, both methods now use func_num_args()/func_get_arg(4): if a 5th argument is still supplied, it is treated as the (now 4th-position) $extra_trusted_interface value and a deprecation notice is triggered rather than a hard fatal. The two now-unused TrustedCallbackInterface constants (THROW_EXCEPTION, TRIGGER_SILENCED_DEPRECATION) are marked @deprecated in their docblocks rather than removed outright, consistent with the Drupal core deprecation policy.

Upgrade

Remove any explicit $error_type argument (TrustedCallbackInterface::THROW_EXCEPTION or TrustedCallbackInterface::TRIGGER_SILENCED_DEPRECATION) from calls to doTrustedCallback() or StaticTrustedCallbackHelper::callback(). If you need to pass $extra_trusted_interface, it is now the 4th argument:

// Before:
$this->doTrustedCallback($callback, $args, $message, TrustedCallbackInterface::THROW_EXCEPTION, RenderCallbackInterface::class);

// After:
$this->doTrustedCallback($callback, $args, $message, RenderCallbackInterface::class);

Untrusted callbacks always throw Drupal\Core\Security\UntrustedCallbackException now; there is no replacement for the silenced-deprecation behavior.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: September 12, 2019
  • Committed: October 1, 2026 (7 years later)

Key contributors

  • xjm
  • dww
  • berdir
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)
  • samuel.mortenson
  • larowlan (PreviousNext)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)

Collaboration

This issue sat postponed for years: in 2020 alexpott argued it shouldn't proceed until #2966711 (trusted callbacks for form arrays) was settled, "possibly never", since contrib might still want the deprecation path for its own callback types. dww and berdir independently reached the same conclusion after digging into core/lib/Drupal/Core/Security/DoTrustedCallbackTrait.php and discovering that Drupal 9's Renderer.php was already unconditionally throwing exceptions, so the issue was really about removing now-dead plumbing rather than closing a live security gap. When larowlan revived the issue in 2025 ahead of Drupal 12, alexpott used a code search across contrib (turning up a real caller in twig_field_value) to confirm that simply deleting the $error_type parameter would break existing code, and added the func_num_args()-based deprecation shim so those callers get a warning instead of a fatal error.

item.title: #3585957: Prevent the navigation sidebar being rendered via big pipe
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.4.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +22/−17 · yml +17/−17 · php +5
  • Diff: 9afec8f
  • Discussion: #3585957 · 6 contributors · 32 comments
  • Followers: 13
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 6 contributors

Summary

When the new navigation sidebar's render cache was cold, Drupal used BigPipe to stream it in after the rest of the page had already loaded. This caused the whole page content to visibly jump sideways as the sidebar popped in, an effect known as content layout shift (jank). This fix stops the navigation sidebar from being deferred via BigPipe, so it renders inline with the rest of the page instead. This can make the initial page response marginally slower on a cache miss, but avoids the jarring layout shift, and testing also showed it slightly reduces the number of separate asset/cache operations needed for the page.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The fix adds #placeholder_strategy_denylist to the navigation render element built in NavigationRenderer::buildNavigation() (core/modules/navigation/src/NavigationRenderer.php), denylisting BigPipeStrategy::class. This is the same mechanism already used elsewhere in core, such as BlockViewBuilder and Core\Render\Element\StatusMessages, to opt a #lazy_builder placeholder out of BigPipe handling via ChainedPlaceholderStrategy. item.title: #3516706: Disallow dangerous filenames e.g. command injection characters
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +76/−3 · php +76/−3
  • Diff: c30d609
  • Discussion: #3516706 · 13 contributors · 96 comments
  • Followers: 24
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 13 contributors

Summary

Drupal now automatically strips a fixed set of dangerous characters, including shell metacharacters like ` $ ; | & `, quotes, angle brackets, control characters, and path separators, from the names of newly uploaded files, replacing them with underscores. This closes off a potential command-injection or XSS vector that could arise if a filename containing such characters was later passed unsafely to a shell command or rendered without escaping. The change applies to every site automatically and cannot be turned off; only newly uploaded files are affected, existing filenames are left untouched. Filenames that would otherwise collapse to nothing (e.g. ... or files with only unsafe characters before the extension) now fall back to unnamed instead of becoming empty, and a leading dash or dot left after sanitization is also handled so the result can't be mistaken for a command-line option or a hidden dotfile. Whitespace in filenames is unaffected, that remains governed by the existing optional filename_sanitization setting.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The logic lives in \Drupal\file\EventSubscriber\SecurityFileUploadEventSubscriber::sanitizeName(), which already ran last in the FileUploadSanitizeNameEvent chain and already stripped null bytes unconditionally, so the new mandatory stripping was added there rather than in the configurable FileEventSubscriber. A new INSECURE_CHARACTERS PCRE constant (built with Unicode property classes \p{Cc} for control characters and \p{Cf} for invisible format/bidi-override characters, plus a literal set of shell metacharacters, quotes, path separators, # and %) is matched and replaced with _ via preg_replace(). After that substitution, a leading - is trimmed (since many CLI tools parse a leading dash as an option), and if the result is empty or starts with . it is prefixed with the FALLBACK_FILENAME constant unnamed, relying on the existing suffixing in FileSystem::createFilename() to disambiguate collisions (unnamed_0, unnamed_1, etc).

The issue went through several design iterations, an earlier approach tried to also default-enable whitespace replacement and made the character list configurable via file.settings, but both were dropped: whitespace substitution was judged too disruptive to ship as a default and was left as the existing opt-in setting, and making the blocked-character list configurable was rejected because a misconfigured list could reintroduce the vulnerability. Characters are now replaced rather than deleted outright, a change from an earlier iteration, so that e.g. Love&War.pdf becomes Love_War.pdf rather than LoveWar.pdf, preserving more of the original separation between words. A related follow-up, #3562543, fixed a crash in the whitespace-replacement regex when fed invalid UTF-8 and landed first as a prerequisite.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: April 1, 2025
  • Committed: September 19, 2026 (1 year later)

Key contributors

  • mcdruid (Acquia)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • cmlara (DM13 Security LLC)
  • kim.pepper (PreviousNext)
  • benjifisher (Harvard Web Publishing)
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • mohit_aghera (PreviousNext)
  • larowlan (PreviousNext)
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)
  • xjm (xjm)

Collaboration

The issue spent over a year iterating on scope. mcdruid (the reporter) and kim.pepper went back and forth on whether to strip a fixed list of "dangerous" characters versus making the list configurable, and whether to default-enable whitespace replacement; a usability team review (summarized by mcdruid in comment #26 and confirmed by benjifisher in #30) concluded that stripping punctuation should be non-negotiable but replacing whitespace should remain an opt-in default. Attempting to flip the whitespace default uncovered an unrelated bug (a preg_replace() call returning null on malformed UTF-8 input), which kim.pepper and mcdruid debugged together and split off into the prerequisite issue #3562543. After that landed, mcdruid disclosed using Claude to help work out the final implementation pushed to the MR, abandoning the configurable, whitespace-replacing approach in favor of a simpler, non-configurable, replace-not-remove scheme. cmlara then pushed back strongly on making the protection non-configurable and on stripping characters that appear in legitimate filenames, arguing it could create a false sense of safety in downstream code and cause reputational issues if parts of filenames like Love&War.pdf were silently dropped. item.title: #2265487: ConfigEntity based lists with items containing non-ascii characters are not sorted correctly
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 11 files, +165/−9 · php +158/−8 · lock +4/−1 · json +3
  • Diff: 8cd44d4
  • Discussion: #2265487 · 16 contributors · 171 comments
  • Followers: 19

Summary

Lists built from configuration entities, such as content type lists, vocabularies, view modes, blocks, and date formats, are now sorted correctly when their labels contain accented or non-ASCII characters (like é, ñ). Previously these items were pushed to the end of alphabetically sorted lists regardless of their actual letter, because the sort relied on a plain byte comparison. As a side effect, embedded numbers now sort numerically too (for example "Format 10x10" before "Format 100x100"), and block labels, which were previously sorted case-sensitively, are now sorted case-insensitively like other config entities.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New Drupal\Core\Utility\NaturalSort::strnatcasecmp() static method, a locale-aware, collation-based drop-in replacement for PHP's strnatcasecmp(), used internally by config entity sort methods.

Technical details

The various ::sort() implementations across config entity classes (ConfigEntityBase, DateFormat, EntityDisplayModeBase, Language, Block, Action) called PHP's byte-wise strnatcasecmp() (or, in Block's case, strcmp()) to order labels, which is locale-unaware and sorts accented characters after all plain ASCII letters. The fix adds a new final class Drupal\Core\Utility\NaturalSort with a static strnatcasecmp(string $string1, string $string2, ?string $langcode = NULL) method that, when the intl extension is loaded, builds (and caches per langcode in a static array) a \Collator for the given or current language and enables Collator::NUMERIC_COLLATION so embedded numbers compare numerically. It falls back to plain strnatcasecmp() when intl isn't available or no langcode can be resolved. All the affected ::sort() methods were updated to call this helper instead of the raw PHP functions.

Getting there took several redesigns. An earlier iteration deprecated ConfigEntityBase::sort() in favor of new sortEntities()/compare() methods and added a symfony/polyfill-intl-icu dependency as a fallback when intl is missing; that version was committed to 11.x, then reverted within hours because Symfony\Polyfill\Intl\Icu\Collator::compare() wasn't actually implemented, which crashed drush cr and any other code path on sites without the intl extension (duplicate issue #3516545). The version that eventually landed drops the polyfill dependency entirely and keeps the original sort() method signatures unchanged, so there is no deprecation and no new required dependency: composer.json only gained a suggest entry for ext-intl.

A follow-up issue, #3624817, tracks adding a NaturalSort::natcasesort() helper and converting other locale-sensitive strnatcasecmp()/strcmp() call sites across core (e.g. SortArray, plugin collection sort helpers) to use this new utility.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">Code that needs locale-aware label sorting can use the new helper instead of PHP's native function:

use Drupal\Core\Utility\NaturalSort;

usort($items, fn($a, $b) => NaturalSort::strnatcasecmp($a->label(), $b->label()));

Install the PHP intl extension (now suggested in composer.json) to get locale-aware collation; without it the method transparently falls back to strnatcasecmp().</upgrade> <parameter name="collaboration">This bug report sat open for nearly a decade and went through several design iterations before landing. longwave raised a performance concern about invoking services inside the sort callback and questioned whether transliteration was the right approach, which led sleitner to switch the implementation to PHP's Collator (comments around #31). After catch committed an iteration that deprecated sort() and added a Symfony polyfill dependency, acbramley discovered it caused a fatal error ("Class Collator not found") on sites without the intl extension because the polyfill's Collator::compare() wasn't implemented; catch reverted the commit the same day and reopened the issue to fix it properly (duplicate #3516545). alexpott then did an extensive review, identified that Collator needed NUMERIC_COLLATION enabled to beat plain strnatcasecmp() even for English sites, and proposed abandoning the sort()/sortEntities() API split in favor of the simpler, purely additive NaturalSort utility class that ultimately shipped, crediting sleitner for "an amazing job of keeping up with all my reviews" across the many reroll and rebase cycles (smustgrave similarly thanked sleitner for "keeping up with all the rebases").</collaboration> <parameter name="ai_disclosures">[]

item.title: #3626470: Review Drupal 12 and 11.x composer dependencies for allowed versions with CVEs
item.description:

Summary

Drupal's composer.json files (root and core/) had their minimum allowed dependency versions raised so that even the lowest versions Composer is willing to resolve are not affected by known CVEs. The runtime dependency guzzlehttp/guzzle now requires at least 8.0.1, and the development-only dependencies composer/composer and phpunit/phpunit had their floors raised too. This is a hardening change with no behavioral effect on a normal composer update: sites that already install recent versions of these libraries are unaffected, but the change closes a gap where composer update --prefer-lowest or a minimal fresh install could previously land on a vulnerable version.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Requirements: Minimum allowed guzzlehttp/guzzle version raised from ^8.0 to ^8.0.1 in core's runtime requirements; dev-only minimums for composer/composer (^2.8.1 to ^2.10.3) and phpunit/phpunit (^12.5.15 to ^12.5.22) were also raised.

Technical details

The issue was triggered by running composer audit --locked combined with composer update --prefer-lowest (with COMPOSER_NO_SECURITY_BLOCKING=1 to bypass Composer's own blocking) to see which CVEs would affect the lowest versions Drupal's constraints technically allow, as opposed to the versions actually pinned in composer.lock. That audit found advisories affecting composer/composer, google/protobuf, guzzlehttp/guzzle, guzzlehttp/psr7, squizlabs/php_codesniffer, and symfony/polyfill-intl-idn at their lowest allowed versions.

The committed fix (d29add7e on main, cherry-picked to 11.x and 12.0.x) bumps the floor for the packages Drupal can actually constrain: guzzlehttp/guzzle from ^8.0 to ^8.0.1 in both root and core/composer.json, and the require-dev minimums for composer/composer (^2.10.3) and phpunit/phpunit (^12.5.22). composer.lock and its content-hash were regenerated to match. google/protobuf and squizlabs/php_codesniffer were left alone since they are transitive dependencies Drupal doesn't declare directly. symfony/polyfill-intl-idn was deliberately left unconstrained: per discussion between gábor hojtsy and xjm, its CVE-2026-46644 is considered a hardening-only issue rather than an exploitable vulnerability, and both the 11.x and main lockfiles already resolve above the affected range, so no explicit version constraint or conflict was added for it.

item.title: #3507570: Allow recipe to add multiple buttons to CKEditor toolbar
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 11.4.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +146/−25 · php +146/−25
  • Diff: c1ccef9
  • Discussion: #3507570 · 9 contributors · 51 comments
  • Followers: 11
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 9 contributors

Summary

Recipes that configure a CKEditor 5 toolbar can now add several buttons in a single step. Previously the addItemToToolbar config action only accepted one toolbar item at a time, so a recipe that needed to add several buttons had to repeat the action once per button. The new addItemsToToolbar action accepts a list of items, each either a button name or an options array (for example to set position or allow_duplicate), and applies them all in one pass.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New hook_config_action_alter() lets modules alter or alias config action plugin definitions, and a new editor:addItemsToToolbar config action adds multiple CKEditor 5 toolbar items in a single recipe action.

Technical details

Drupal\ckeditor5\Plugin\ConfigAction\AddItemToToolbar::apply() now normalizes its $value argument: a plain string or an associative array is treated as a single item and wrapped in a list, while an indexed array is treated as multiple items. Each item is delegated to a new private applySingle() method, which contains the original per-item logic (position, replace, allow_duplicate, plugin default configuration), and the editor entity is saved only once at the end if anything actually changed. Invalid input, an empty list, a non-string/array item, or an item missing item_name, now throws a ConfigActionException with a descriptive message instead of failing a silent assert().

Because the #[ConfigAction] attribute isn't repeatable, the plural addItemsToToolbar isn't a second plugin class: it's registered as an alias of editor:addItemToToolbar inside Ckeditor5Hooks::configActionAlter(), which implements the new hook_config_action_alter() documented in core.api.php. That hook receives the config action plugin definitions array by reference and lets any module copy or alter entries, here it copies the editor:addItemToToolbar definition to a new editor:addItemsToToolbar key and gives it its own admin_label. Maintainers noted in review that using an alter hook for aliasing is a stopgap that decouples the plural action from its singular definition, and that dedicated alias support on the ConfigAction attribute would be a cleaner long term solution, left as a followup.

Upgrade

To add multiple CKEditor 5 toolbar buttons in a recipe, replace repeated addItemToToolbar calls with a single addItemsToToolbar call taking a list:

config:
  actions:
    editor.editor.content_format:
      addItemsToToolbar:
        - specialCharacters
        - codeBlock
        -
          item_name: italic
          position: 0
          allow_duplicate: true

Modules can also implement hook_config_action_alter(array &$definitions) to alias or otherwise alter any config action plugin definition, not just this one.

item.title: #3465228: Twig disallows dashes in variable names, so SDC should disallow it in prop names and slots

  • Followers: 19

Summary

Single Directory Components (SDC) prop and slot names are now validated to ensure they are usable as Twig variables. Because Twig compiles a dash in a variable name as a subtraction operator, a prop or slot named something like test-required-string silently broke templates instead of producing a clear error, costing developers debugging time. Component definitions with prop or slot names that don't start with a letter or underscore and continue with letters, digits, or underscores now fail validation immediately with a clear error message, rather than failing confusingly at render time. Variant names are unaffected, since they are used as string values (e.g. CSS modifiers) and never become Twig variable or block names.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Single Directory Component (SDC) prop and slot names must now match ^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$ (valid Twig/PHP identifiers); previously dashes and other characters were tolerated even though they never worked correctly in Twig templates.

Because prop names are validated against a JSON Schema draft version (draft-04, via justinrainbow) that lacks propertyNames support, ComponentValidator::validateDefinition() in core/lib/Drupal/Core/Theme/Component/ComponentValidator.php also gained an explicit PHP-side check: it filters $prop_names against /^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$/ and throws InvalidComponentException up front, before falling through to the JSON Schema validator, when it finds a name that doesn't match. This gives an explicit "Prop names must match the pattern..." error instead of a validator error that's harder to trace back to the actual cause.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">Rename any SDC prop or slot names that contain dashes, spaces, or a leading digit to use only letters, digits, and underscores, starting with a letter or underscore:

  properties:

      type: string

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: dblog_update_12100() deletes any rows with a negative wid and converts the watchdog.wid primary key column to an unsigned big integer, matching the schema as actually declared.
  • Deprecation: Returning a legacy array from hook_schema() (rather than a Drupal\Core\Database\SchemaDefinition\Schema object) to ModuleInstaller::installSchema()/uninstallSchema() or to SchemaInspector::getTablesSpecification() is deprecated in drupal:12.1.0 and will be removed in drupal:13.0.0.

Technical details

The converted hook_schema() implementations now build a Schema object out of Table, Column, Index, PrimaryKey, and ForeignKey value objects (e.g. Column::varcharAscii(name: 'entity_type', length: EntityTypeInterface::ID_MAX_LENGTH, ...)) instead of returning nested PHP arrays. ModuleInstaller::installSchema() and uninstallSchema() now call @trigger_error(..., E_USER_DEPRECATED) whenever a module's _schema() hook returns anything other than a Schema instance (and the array is non-empty), pointing to https://www.drupal.org/node/3557405.

Validation was tightened on the SchemaDefinition value objects themselves: Column::validate() now throws a SchemaDefinitionException if length is missing for Varchar/VarcharAscii columns, Schema::validate() rejects duplicate table names, and Table::validate() (via a new columnNames() method) rejects duplicate column names within a table.

The conversion surfaced a real discrepancy: dblog_schema()'s watchdog.wid was declared unsigned: TRUE under the new definition, but the live database column was not actually enforced as unsigned. dblog_update_12100() removes any rows with negative wid values and runs changeField() to make the column unsigned, with a new UpdatePathTest exercising the negative-id-then-update scenario. Conversion of schemata defined by test modules was explicitly postponed to a follow-up issue, per review feedback from amateescu, to keep this change reviewable.

Upgrade

Module maintainers should convert their hook_schema() implementations from arrays to SchemaDefinition objects to avoid deprecation notices, for example:

function mymodule_schema(): Schema {
  $tables[] = new Table(
    name: 'mymodule_table',
    description: '...',
    columns: [
      Column::int(
        name: 'id',
        description: '...',
        unsigned: TRUE,
        notNull: TRUE,
        default: new IntValue(0),
      ),
    ],
    primaryKey: new PrimaryKey(['id']),
  );

  return new Schema(
    type: SchemaDefinitionType::Module,
    name: 'mymodule',
    tables: $tables,
  );
}

Sites with existing dblog data will have their watchdog.wid column corrected to unsigned via dblog_update_12100() when running database updates.

item.title: #3625969: Twig's 3.30 TypeError: Twig\Runtime\EscaperRuntime::escape(): Argument #4 ($autoescape) must be of type bool, null given
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Critical bug report
  • Version: 10.6.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +72/−14 · php +72/−14
  • Diff: b4659e2
  • Discussion: #3625969 · 21 contributors · 53 comments
  • Followers: 55

Summary

Twig 3.30 changed how its escape/e filter compiles, and Drupal's mechanism for swapping in its own MarkupInterface-aware escaping broke as a result: every templated page threw a TypeError and produced a white screen of death. This fix restores compatibility so sites can run Drupal with Twig 3.30 (or Twig 3.28/3.29) without the crash. Anyone who had pinned twig/twig to an older version as a workaround can lift that pin once they update to a core release containing this fix.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Twig 3.30 introduced a dedicated EscapeFilter node that compiles directly to $this->escaper->escape(...). Drupal's TwigNodeVisitor::leaveNode() previously handled escape/e filters by swapping the compiled node's callable to Drupal's own drupal_escape filter, but leaving Twig's own EscapeFilter node in place to build the call. Twig 3.30 still emitted the direct escaper->escape() call, but built its arguments for drupal_escape (which needs the environment as its first parameter), so $this->env was inserted as an extra leading argument, every other argument shifted over, and null (the charset) ended up in the $autoescape boolean slot.

Rather than swapping the callable on Twig's own escape node at parse time, TwigExtension::getFilters() now registers Drupal's escapeFilter method directly under the names escape and e (in addition to drupal_escape), reusing a shared $escape_options array. Because Twig loads Drupal's extension after its own EscaperExtension, and later-registered filters of the same name win, Twig's built-in escape node/filter is overridden outright and never compiled, so the argument-shifting bug can't occur regardless of Twig version. A new TwigExtension::escapeFilterIsSafe() static method replaces the previous reliance on Twig's internal twig_escape_filter_is_safe helper as the is_safe_callback. TwigNodeVisitor::leaveNode() was simplified accordingly: it no longer swaps the node's callable, it just checks whether the filter name is escape, e, or drupal_escape to set $this->skipRenderVarFunction. A new testEscapeFilterOverride() test in TwigExtensionTest asserts that both explicit (|escape, |e) and automatic escaping compile to Drupal's own escapeFilter method.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">

item.title: #3581349: Remove Syndicate block config
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 12.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +158/−0 · php +96 · yml +62
  • Diff: be4d779
  • Discussion: #3581349 · 5 contributors · 21 comments
  • Followers: 5
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

The Syndicate block (the RSS feed icon block) was deprecated in Drupal 11.2 with no replacement and its plugin code was removed ahead of Drupal 12. That left orphaned block.block.* configuration on any site that still had the block placed. Running database updates to Drupal 12.0.0 now automatically deletes that leftover block configuration, in any theme, not just Olivero where the block originally lived.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: New block_post_update_remove_syndicate_blocks() post update deletes any block.block.* configuration using the removed node_syndicate_block plugin whose settings.provider is node, in any theme.

Technical details

The fix adds block_post_update_remove_syndicate_blocks() in core/modules/block/block.post_update.php, which loads all block config entities with plugin set to node_syndicate_block and settings.provider set to node, and deletes them. Restricting the match to settings.provider: node (rather than just the plugin ID) means a block config entity that a contrib or custom module has taken over, for example by changing its provider, such as the stark_custom_syndicate fixture with provider: custom_syndicate, is left alone.

Test coverage was added in BlockRemoveSyndicateBlocksUpdateTest, using new fixtures (block.block.olivero_syndicate.yml, block.block.stark_syndicate.yml, block.block.stark_custom_syndicate.yml) loaded via a new syndicate-block-config.php update fixture script, verifying that Syndicate blocks in both Olivero and Stark are removed while the provider-overridden block and unrelated blocks survive the update. The related issue #3518990 originally deprecated the SyndicateBlock plugin before its removal in core.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: March 25, 2026
  • Committed: September 24, 2026 (6 months later)

Key contributors

  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • catch (Third and Grove)
  • xjm (Zoocha)
  • gábor hojtsy (Acquia)
  • godotislate

Collaboration

catch traced the history of the change (deprecation in #3518990, code removal in #3571623) and laid out the tradeoff: leave the zombie config with a release note telling sites to check for it, or add an update to delete it outright, at the risk that some site is still relying on it. Gábor Hojtsy reasoned that because the code removal had only ever landed on the main branch and never in a released version, no site could yet have taken ownership of the config by reimplementing the plugin, which made it safe to delete now; he then opened the merge request implementing the deletion. xjm pushed for a more discoverable change record rather than relying on release notes alone, and catch added one before the fix was committed.
